narrative.text: A portrait photograph of a woman with short grey curly hair wearing a red scarf over a blue patterned top. The surrounding text identifies her as Dr Soumya Swaminathan, Chief Scientist, WHO, author of the Foreword.

A decorative graphic showing a stylized world map rendered in glowing blue tones, overlaid with a bright cyan heartbeat (ECG) waveform line running horizontally across it and a white medical caduceus (staff with wings) symbol at the center.

A very small, plain light-blue circular icon with no discernible internal detail; its specific content could not be determined from the extracted image. It appears alongside a list of key WHO source documents (National eHealth Strategy Toolkit, WHO guideline on digital interventions) and functions as a minor decorative or bullet-style graphic element rather than a substantive figure.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for sections presenting individual Principles for Digital Development, here principle 3, 'Be collaborative'.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for this page's two principles, 'Understand the existing ecosystem' and 'Design with the user'.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for this page's two principles, 'Use open standards, open data, open source, and open innovation' and 'Reuse and improve'.

A screenshot of the WHO Digital Health Atlas web application, showing a map of parts of East Africa (South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia, Uganda, Kenya, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi) with numbered blue pin markers indicating counts of cataloged digital health implementations at each location (values visible include 2, 4, 6, 30, 34 and 83). A side panel lists implementations for Rwanda, including 'E-Heza Data Solutions', 'Rwanda Health Analytics Platform (RHAP)', 'Rwanda HMIS' and 'DHIS2 for COVID-19 Surveillance', with a toggle to switch the map between 'Sub-national' and 'National' views.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for principle 8, 'Build for sustainability'.

The OpenHIM logo: a green double-chevron (forward-arrow) icon beside the wordmark 'OpenHIM'. It represents one of the three component technologies, an interoperability layer for standards-compliant health information exchange, shown as part of Fig. 5.6.2 illustrating how mHero integrates digital health interventions using standards.

The iHRIS logo: a colorful aperture/lens-style icon beside the wordmark 'iHRIS'. It represents one of the three component technologies, an open source health workforce information system, shown as part of Fig. 5.6.2 illustrating how mHero integrates digital health interventions using standards.

The OpenHIE logo: a teal and blue circular/plus-shaped icon beside the wordmark 'OpenHIE'. It represents the interoperability framework referenced in Fig. 5.6.2, which illustrates how mHero integrates digital health interventions using standards.

The RapidPro logo: a small blue square icon beside the wordmark 'RapidPro'. It represents one of the three component technologies, an open source interactive messaging platform, shown as part of Fig. 5.6.2 illustrating how mHero integrates digital health interventions using standards.

The mHero logo: the wordmark 'mHero' in blue and grey text with a small wifi/signal-style icon. mHero is the combined communication tool described on the page, built from iHRIS, RapidPro and OpenHIM, shown as a component of Fig. 5.6.2 illustrating how mHero integrates digital health interventions using standards.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for the principle 'Reuse and improve'.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for the principle 'Design for scale'.

The 'Principles for Digital Development' logo: an irregular grid of solid colored squares (blue, green, orange, red, dark teal, light blue) arranged asymmetrically, used as a recurring header graphic for the principle 'Be data driven'.

A standard ISBN barcode (EAN-13) reading 9789240010567, printed with the number both above the bars and split beneath them ('9', '789240', '010567'). It appears on the document's final page as a back-cover administrative element with no page text.
